seller_questions: What is the engine number, and can you photograph the engine-number stamping on the case?
Do you have any service invoices for this car? Please send copies, especially any water pump, coolant tank, AOS, clutch, IMS or RMS work with dates and mileages.
Will you allow an independent Porsche-specialist PPI with a borescope of all six cylinders before any deposit, and which nearby shop do you recommend or permit?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, after sitting overnight, filmed from the rear with the engine cover visible for the first 30 seconds?
Can you send a Durametric or PIWIS scan showing stored faults and cam deviation values for both banks?
What are the DOT date codes and brands on all four tires?
Can you send photos of the underside, including the RMS/bellhousing area, the coolant tank, and both front radiators with the bumper lower grilles removed?
Can you send a video of the top cycling fully down and up, plus photos of the drain channels and lifted footwell carpet edges?
Can you share the full AutoCheck or Carfax report, including the states the car was registered in and the ownership dates?
Is the car on its original clutch, and does it judder from a stop?
Is there any oil consumption or oil top-up history between changes?
Is the $33,890 negotiable given that comparable 987.1 S sales are well below it?
ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders for bore scoring, with particular attention to the bank 2 (cylinders 4-6) thrust sides on this 3.4 M97.
Cut the oil filter and inspect the media for metallic debris (IMS and bearing wear); confirm the engine number and bearing type.
Durametric scan: fault memory, cam deviation values, and over-rev counts by range.
Cold-start listening test for piston slap, chain rattle or VarioCam noise; check for startup smoke (AOS).
RMS and AOS leaks on the bellhousing and underside; any oil on the transmission.
Cooling: water pump weep, expansion tank crust, and front radiator/condenser corrosion and debris packing.
Underside corrosion given a possible New England history: subframes, brake lines, coolant pipes.
Convertible top cycle, cables and hydraulic rams; drains, footwell dampness and seat/top control modules.
Clutch engagement point and DMF judder; front control arms, coffin-arm bushings and top mounts.
Tire date codes and brand match; paint-meter readings under the PPF and on all panels.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean Porsche-specialist borescope, clean oil filter, clean scan and the engine number, plus a meaningful price reduction toward the fair value range.
Up: invoices showing cooling-system renewal, IMS/RMS/clutch work or regular oil service history.
Down: any bore scoring, metallic filter debris, high over-rev counts or cam deviation out of spec.
Down: dealer refusal of an independent PPI, or underside rust or coolant/oil leaks found at inspection.
evidence.mission_note: It is a manual with real character, but at this asking price it sits above the $27,000 bridge ceiling. The profile also frames the 987 as a keeper choice, and 3.4 M97 bore-scoring exposure undercuts the 'reliable, easy resale' bridge brief unless a borescope clears it.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly to a 2008 Boxster S 3.4 convertible, photos confirm a 6-speed manual, and the AutoCheck summary shows clean title, 0 reported accidents and 2 owners. Photos show good cosmetics, including front PPF, red calipers, 19-inch Turbo wheels, bi-xenons, an intact top and a tidy black interior. None of the model-critical evidence is present: no service records, engine number, IMS documentation, borescope, filter inspection, scan or cooling receipts. That gap matters most because this is a 2007-2008 3.4 M97, the variant with the highest bore-scoring exposure, and it likely has the non-retrofittable large IMS bearing. The one observed issue is price: $33,890 including fees is well above the fair value range of $19,743–$26,114 and above the $27,000 max_price in the state block. Underside and drain condition are open questions given the Massachusetts location, and tire dates and warning-light status are not examined here. Low mileage does not establish age-related service on an 18-year-old car.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer for the engine number, any service invoices, a cold-start video and written permission for an independent Porsche-specialist PPI with borescope in the Topsfield area, then reassess with that evidence and a price counter.
